explain.say: Drop it into a drink and the outer layer warms up quickly. Like most solids, ice expands slightly as it warms, so the outside tries to get bigger.

faq.q: Why does uneven warming crack ice?
faq.a: The warm outside expands while the cold inside does not, so parts of the cube push and pull on each other. Brittle ice cannot stretch, so it cracks. This is called thermal shock.

faq.q: Why do ice cubes make a cracking sound?
faq.a: The sound comes from cracks suddenly running through the brittle ice, and from small bubbles of trapped air escaping as the ice splits and melts.

faq.q: Why are some ice cubes cloudy?
faq.a: Ice freezes from the outside in, pushing dissolved air and minerals towards the middle, where they get trapped as tiny bubbles. The bubbles scatter light and look white.
asks: Why is the middle of ice white?

faq.q: Do ice cubes crack more in warm drinks?
faq.a: Yes. The bigger the temperature difference between the ice and the drink, the faster the surface warms and the bigger the stress.
asks: Does warm water make ice crack more?

faq.q: Why does a cold glass sometimes crack with boiling water?
faq.a: It is the same thermal shock. The inside surface heats and expands quickly while the outside stays cool, and the stress can crack ordinary glass.
asks: Why do glasses crack with hot water?

facts: Ice expands about four times as much per degree of warming as steel does.
A home freezer is usually set to about minus 18 degrees Celsius.
